plain_english: Now the unification, arrived in due course, is discussed.
sanskrit_cite: athāvasarasaṃprāpta ekīkāro nigadyate

plain_english: Since it was said the triad is to be worshipped together with the cakra-divisions: here, in this manner, is their unification.
sanskrit_cite: yaduktaṃ cakrabhedena sārdhaṃ pūjyamiti trikam | tatraiṣa cakrabhedānāmekīkāro diśānayā

plain_english: Viśvā, her Mistress, Hāraudrī, Vīranetrī, Ambikā, and Gurvī, thus: the goddesses shown in the Siddhāvīra, in the six-spoked wheel.
sanskrit_cite: viśvā tadīśā hāraudrī vīranetryambikā tathā | gurvīti ṣaḍare devyaḥ śrīsiddhāvīradarśitāḥ

plain_english: Māheśī, Brāhmaṇī, Skāndī, Vaiṣṇavī, Aindrī, Yamātmikā, Cāmuṇḍā indeed, and Yogīśī — thus eight, or the Aghorī-group and the rest.
sanskrit_cite: māheśī brāhmaṇī skāndī vaiṣṇavyaindrī yamātmikā | cāmuṇḍā caiva yogīśītyaṣṭāghoryādayo@thavā

plain_english: Joined with the twelve — the mothers of Fire, Nirṛti, Wind, and Īśa: Nandā, Bhadrā, Jayā, Kālī, Karālī, Vikṛtānanā.
sanskrit_cite: agninirṛtivāyvīśamātṛbhirdvādaśānvitāḥ | nandā bhadrā jayā kālī karālī vikṛtānanā

plain_english: Kroṣṭukī and Bhīmamudrā, Vāyuvegā, Hayānanā, Gambhīrā, and Ghoṣaṇī, thus: the rule in the twenty-four-spoked wheel.
sanskrit_cite: kroṣṭukī bhīmamudrā ca vāyuvegā hayānanā | gambhīrā ghoṣaṇī ceti caturviṃśatyare vidhiḥ

plain_english: Siddhi, Vṛddhi, Dyuti, Lakṣmī, Medhā, Kānti, Sudhā, Dhṛti, Dīpti, Puṣṭi, Mati, Kīrti, Susthiti, Sugati, Smṛti.
sanskrit_cite: siddhirvṛddhirdyutirlakṣmīrmedhā kāntiḥ sudhā dhṛtiḥ | dīptiḥ puṣṭirmatiḥ kīrtiḥ susthitiḥ sugatiḥ smṛtiḥ

plain_english: Suprabhā — sixteen in all, thus: the Śrīkaṇṭha-headed powers. Bali and Balinanda, Daśagrīva, Hara, Haya.
sanskrit_cite: suprabhā ṣoḍaśī ceti śrīkaṇṭhādikaśaktayaḥ | baliśca balinandaśca daśagrīvo haro hayaḥ

plain_english: Mādhava in the six-spoked wheel; but in the twelve-spoked these are remembered: Dakṣa, Caṇḍa, Hara, Śauṇḍī, Pramatha, Bhīma and Manmatha.
sanskrit_cite: mādhavaḥ ṣaḍare cakre dvādaśāre tvamī smṛtāḥ | dakṣaścaṇḍo haraḥ śauṇḍī pramatho bhīmamanmathau

plain_english: Śakuni, Sumati, Nanda, Gopāla and Pitāmaha; Śrīkaṇṭha, Ananta, Sūkṣma, and Trimūrti, Śaṃbareśvara.
sanskrit_cite: śakuniḥ sumatirnando gopālaśca pitāmahaḥ | śrīkaṇṭho@nantasūkṣmau ca trimūrtiḥ śaṃbareśvaraḥ

plain_english: Arghīśa and Bhārabhūti, Sthiti, Sthāṇu, Hara, thus; Jhaṇṭi, Bhautika, Sadyoja, Anugraha, Krūra, Sainika.
sanskrit_cite: arghīśo bhārabhūtiśca sthitiḥ sthāṇurharastathā | jhaṇṭhibhautikasadyojānugrahakrūrasainikāḥ

plain_english: Two-eight; whatever nectar, joined therewith: Pūrṇa, Ābha and their fluids, Ogha, Ūrmi, Syandana, Aṅga, and Vapus, Udgāra, Vaktraka.
sanskrit_cite: dvyaṣṭau yadvāmṛtastena yuktāḥ pūrṇābhataddravāḥ | oghormisyandanāṅgāśca vapurudgāravaktrakāḥ

plain_english: Tanu, Secana, Mūrti, Īśa; Sarvāmṛtadhara, and the other; by feminine reading these powers are declared sixteen indeed.
sanskrit_cite: tanusecanamūrtīśāḥ sarvāmṛtadharo@paraḥ | śrīpāṭhācchaktayaścaitāḥ ṣoḍaśaiva prakīrtitāḥ

plain_english: Saṃvarta, Lakulī, Bhṛgu, Sita, Baka, Khaṅgī, Pinākī, Bhujaga, Bali, Kāla; Dvi and Chagalāṇḍa; Śikhī, Śoṇa, Meṣa, Mīna, Tridaṇḍī; with Āṣāḍhī.
sanskrit_cite: saṃvartalakulibhṛgusitabakakhaṅgipinākibhujagabalikālāḥ | dviśchagalāṇḍau śikhiśoṇameṣamīnatridaṇḍi sāṣāḍhi

plain_english: Devīkānta and his half; Dāruka, Hali, Somanātha, Śarman; Jaya, Vijaya, Jayantā, Jita, Sujaya, Jaya, the Rudrakīrtana-bringers.
sanskrit_cite: devīkāntatadardhau dārukahalisomanāthaśarmāṇaḥ | jayavijayajayantājitasujayajayarudrakīrtanāvahakāḥ

plain_english: Increasing zeal for His form; and the Bala, Subala, Bhadra gift-bearers; its bearer and giver, and the Lord, joyous, equal, blessed of His form.
sanskrit_cite: tanmūrtyutsāhadavardhanāśca balasubalabhadradāvahakāḥ | tadvāndātā ceśo nandanasamabhadratanmūrtiḥ

plain_english: Desiring well-minded Śiva-giving; Durga, time called Bhadra, mind-following Kauśika, Kāla, Viśva, Suśivās and others likewise; Kopa.
sanskrit_cite: śivadasumanaḥspṛhaṇakā durgo bhadrākhyakālaśca | ceto@nugakauśikakālaviśvasuśivāstathāparaḥ kopaḥ

plain_english: On the ear-fire spoke these would be; by feminine reading these are śaktis. 'Juṃkāra' and 'Agnipatnī', thus, in the six-spoked, eunuch-excluded.
sanskrit_cite: śrutyagnyare syurete strīpāṭhācchaktayastvetāḥ | juṃkāro@thāgnipatnīti ṣaḍare ṣaṇṭhavarjitāḥ

plain_english: In the twelve-spoked, those along with them; in the sixteen-spoked, the vowels in order; ha in the twice-eight-spoked; from ya to the ha-end, but, in the trika.
sanskrit_cite: dvādaśāre tatsahitāḥ ṣoḍaśāre svarāḥ kramāt | halastaddviguṇe@ṣṭāre yādyaṃ hāntaṃ tu tattrike

plain_english: On the thirty-two-spoked, with end, bindu on the head of all; thus many other cakra-divisions one should construct from this.
sanskrit_cite: dvātriṃśadarake sāntaṃ binduḥ sarveṣu mūrdhani | evamanyānbahūṃścakrabhedānasmātprakalpayet

plain_english: One alone is this consciousness-self, the essence of universe-awareness; śakti and her possessor thence — mother, mass of sound — are declared a pair.
sanskrit_cite: eka eva cidātmaiṣa viśvāmarśanasārakaḥ | śaktistadvānato mātā śabdarāśiḥ prakīrtitau

plain_english: But in the division of those two, in the fashioning of śakti and her possessor: the sound-mass and Mālinī, of agitation-nature, such a body.
sanskrit_cite: tayoreva vibhāge tu śaktitadvatprakalpane | śabdarāśirmālinī ca kṣobhātma vapurīdṛśam

plain_english: Thus in the splitting of inner awareness, really the triad called Anuttara, Icchā, Unmeṣa — from which the universe is awareness.
sanskrit_cite: tathāntaḥsthaparāmarśabhedane vastutastrikam | anuttarecchonmeṣākhyaṃ yato viśvaṃ vimarśanam

plain_english: But in union with Ānanda, Īśa, Ūrmi, that is declared the hexad; through semivowel-sibilant union that is declared the octad.
sanskrit_cite: ānandeśormiyoge tu tatṣaṭkaṃ samudāhṛtam | antaḥsthoṣmasamāyogāttadaṣṭakamudāhṛtam

plain_english: Then, in the absence of the four amṛta-vowels, it would be a dodecad; in union with them, called sixteen — thus until innumerability.
sanskrit_cite: tadāmṛtacatuṣkonabhāve dvādaśakaṃ bhavet | tadyoge ṣoḍaśākhyaṃ syādevaṃ yāvadasaṃkhyatā

plain_english: Since it clearly bears the universe from single-awareness-bearing on, bearing part-of-part awarenesses at the end.
sanskrit_cite: viśvamekaparāmarśasahatvātprabhṛti sphuṭam | aṃśāṃśikāparāmarśān paryante sahate yataḥ

plain_english: Hence the fifty's oneness, vowel-manifest-variety, eight vargas, letter-division, eighty-one kalā-rise.
sanskrit_cite: ataḥ pañcāśadaikātmyaṃ svaravyaktivirūpatā | vargāṣṭakaṃ varṇabheda ekāśītikalodayaḥ

plain_english: Thus shown before, from half-mora-bearing; for even vowel-half exists, of the svarita a half-mora.
sanskrit_cite: iti pradarśitaṃ pūrvam ardhamātrāsahatvataḥ | svarārdhamapyasti yataḥ svaritasyārdhamātrakam

plain_english: From its beginning the udātta, that said by the pada-knower; thus this consciousness, of sacrificand-form-awareness-nature.
sanskrit_cite: tasyādita udāttaṃ tatkathitaṃ padavedinā | itthaṃ saṃvidiyaṃ yājyasvarūpāmarśarūpiṇī

plain_english: Unbroken from consciousness, this wheel-horizon of wheels; by lordship-and-veil division employ it manifoldly.
sanskrit_cite: abhinnaṃ saṃvidaścaitaccakrāṇāṃ cakravālakam | svāmyāvaraṇabhedena bahudhā tatprayojayet

plain_english: Parāparā, Parā, and the other: creation, maintenance, concealment; but the fourth, Mātṛsadbhāva-formed, is called repose.
sanskrit_cite: parāparā parā cānyā sṛṣṭisthititirodhayaḥ | mātṛsadbhāvarūpā tu turyā viśrāntirucyate

plain_english: And that clearly mouth-seated, hinted at each word; in the Fourth, repose is to be placed, moving in Mātṛsadbhāva.
sanskrit_cite: tacca prakāśaṃ vaktrasthaṃ sūcitaṃ tu pade pade | turye viśrāntirādheyā mātṛsadbhāvasāriṇi

plain_english: So to him the universe shines, gone to identity with his own self; thus told is this unification of the scripture's matter, uttered by the guru.
sanskrit_cite: tathāsya viśvamābhāti svātmatanmayatāṃ gatam | ityeṣa śāstrārthasyokta ekīkāro gurūditaḥ
